thread:
morgan: @here P0 from CS — hosted API returning 503s for a single customer starting ~08:13 UTC. Upstream runner processes are exiting with SIGSEGV (exit code 139). Billing spike because retries are piling up. Anyone available to triage?
oncall-bot: Escalation created INC-2026-432 and paging oncall.
sara: on it, grabbing logs and a minimal repro from support case.
morgan: support case C-7741. CS says ~80% of requests are 503 in the window and latency was creeping up before the failures.
kai: quick glance at runner logs shows repeated "free(): invalid pointer" followed by segfault. also a few nvml driver resets around the same time. dropping a snippet.
sara: ```[2026-03-17T08:13:02Z] runner[pid=2245]: free(): invalid pointer
[2026-03-17T08:13:03Z] signal: SIGSEGV (code=0) at 0x7f9c2a1b4f00 /app/libtorch.so
[2026-03-17T08:13:04Z] infer: container exited code 139, restarting...```
alice: hmmm could be heap corruption from the kv-cache prefetch path or from buffer reuse when streaming is active. any recent changes deployed?
morgan: customer workload details from CS: average context ~6k tokens but spikes to ~12k with streaming + tool-call expansion. they increased max_tokens in their client yesterday.
ryan: can we repro in staging with same model + quantization flags? I can spin up a repro rig but need the exact prompt and a script.
sara: uploaded a minimal repro tarball to /tmp/repro-acuta.tar.gz and attached the curl command to the case: ```curl -X POST https://staging.redwood/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d @payload.json``` payload.json uses long system messages and multiple function calls to trigger long contexts.
kai: immediate mitigation I suggest: route this key to the low-memory quantized model variant and enable a concurrency circuit breaker for the key. That should reduce memory pressure immediately. tradeoff = slight quality delta.
support-jen: @morgan please check with the customer before we swap models — they flagged hallucination risk with smaller models yesterday.
morgan: will confirm with CS. For now I'll ask infra/runtime to enable a failover route (fallback to quantized) and set concurrency cap to 20% of previous. Who can push the routing change?
alice: I can push the routing policy patch to prod now with an immediate rollback if anything looks off. deploying in ~2m.
oncall-bot: Deployment queued by alice: routing-policy/2026-03-17/patch-128.
alice: policy live. monitoring metrics and OOM/segfaults.
kai: after routing change error rate for that key dropped from ~80% to ~5% within 3 minutes. still seeing occasional segfaults on other tenants — probably a latent memory corruption. I'll open a kernel-debug job to capture sanitized cores.
ryan: I'll collect core dumps from the affected runner instances and try ASAN / debug-build repro on a dev GPU box. also verifying libtorch/libc versions pinned in the image.
morgan: action items: (1) CS to inform customer and confirm acceptance of temporary routing, (2) infra/runtime to collect cores and run ASAN repros, (3) runtime team to audit kv-prefetch/free() and buffer reuse code paths. I'll update INC-2026-432 and the support case.
support-jen: CS notified customer; they accepted the temporary routing and asked for ETA on a permanent fix. CS will update ticket.
morgan: thanks all — keeping thread here for updates. :thumbsup:
